title: Cascade dev onboarding - SDK auth, console & Optimize walkthrough
summary: AE + SE walked Cascade through Redwood SDK quickstart (Python + TS), auth patterns, Console onboarding, and Optimize recommendations. Customer liked the console cost/latency breakdowns but asked for SOC2/kms docs and a private deployment feasibility note. Agreed to run a small latency/cost benchmark on their sample workload and share sandbox keys.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-29 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood CSM); Jordan, Priya, Sam (Cascade)

Auto Summary (auto-generated): quick demo of SDKs, environment setup, auth; walked Console and Optimize; security Qs; agreed pilot + docs + benchmark.

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE on this account, and with me is Maya, our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Jordan: Good thanks, excited to see the walkthrough. We've been poking at the API docs but want the real dev flow.
[00:12] Maya: Awesome. We'll run through a short python quickstart then show the TS example, then flip to Console and Optimize recommendations.
[00:20] Priya: Sounds good. We have a couple constraints: PCI-ish data, need control of keys, and latency under 150ms p50 for short prompts.
[00:30] Alex: Helpful. We'll call out dedicated/private options and KMS integration. Quick note, if we need private deployment we can talk about our VPC package and on prem shim.
[00:40] Sam: And SOC2 evidence — that will be a gating item for security review.
[00:46] Maya: Totally. We'll share the security binder after the call.
[00:50] [01:00] Maya: Ok switching to the screen: first the python quickstart. pip install redwood-client (note: transcription sometimes shows redwood-client as redwood-cli).
[01:12] Maya: Basic snippet: from redwood import RedwoodClient; client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_KEY']) — we show setting env var in CI.
[01:25] Priya: Quick question, how do you rotate credentials in CI? Our current practice is short-lived tokens from our vault.
[01:31] Maya: Great, we support both long-lived keys and short-lived tokens via our token exchange endpoint; many teams put keys into vaults and rotate monthly — we have a sample repo for Hashi/Vault.
[01:45] Jordan: Is there an SDK for typescript that mirrors the python surface?
[01:49] Maya: Yes, TS has the same model api: import { Redwood } from '@redwood/inference' — again small mismatch in package name in older docs — use @redwood/inference.
[02:05] [02:15] Alex: While Maya finishes TS, quick architecture note: we have Console to create routes (you can pin model versions, set batching, and add fallbacks). With Optimize we provide batching/quantization suggestions per-route based on your token distribution.
[02:30] Tessa: For our internal infra, we'd most likely do Dedicated with autoscale; curious on burst behavior — how seamless is fallback to hosted?
[02:41] Maya: We can route by policy: burst to hosted, or degrade to a smaller quantized variant. We'll demo the routing rules in Console.
[02:54] [03:05] Maya: Ok console view: here's Projects -> Sandbox -> Routes. You can see per-route token cost, p50/p95 latency. The UI also surfaces Optimize suggestions like 'enable batching size 8' or 'quantize to 4-bit for this model class'.
[03:23] Priya: Those cost numbers—are they estimates or live billing?
[03:27] Alex: Live token-level accounting but can be delayed by a minute or so; the Console ties into usage billing and our billing exports.
[03:35] [03:45] Jordan: On the privacy side, if we use Dedicated and VPC, where do logs live? We want audit logs in our SIEM not Redwood's cloud.
[03:53] Liam: Good question. For Private/VPC we can forward audit logs to your endpoints, or provide long retention for enterprise packages. We also support bringing your own KMS so tokens never leave your HSM.
[04:10] Sam: That BYOK/KMS part — is it available for dedicated or only private?
[04:14] Maya: BYOK is supported for Private deployments; for Dedicated we have KMS integrations but keys are managed per-tenant with strict access. We'll detail that in the security doc.
[04:25] [04:35] Priya: Back to SDK: when using batching, how do we ensure latency SLOs are honored? We can't have 200ms p50 turn into 1s because of batching.
[04:43] Maya: Right — Optimize suggests batching knobs based on workload, and Console can set per-route max batching latency and timeouts. You can enable continuous batching but cap latency. Often teams set max_batch_latency_ms to 50ms for low-latency apps.
[04:58] Jordan: Can we control kernel selection or model quantization per route?
[05:04] Maya: Yes, you can pin a quantized variant of a model in the route config. The runtime will pick optimized kernels by sequence length; there can be small transcriptions in the docs where model names are slightly off.
[05:18] [05:30] Alex: I'll pause for a sec — any blockers for you on using our hosted API for dev vs starting with Dedicated?
[05:38] Priya: We'd like dev on hosted but production on Dedicated if numbers look good. Main blocker is SOC2 and KMS assurances.
[05:46] Sam: Also data residency—we have EU customer data we need kept in eu-west-1.
[05:51] Maya: We have region pinning for hosted endpoints and Dedicated in specific regions; for full EU residency we'd advise Private deployment but many customers use Dedicated in eu-west-1.
[06:04] [06:10] Maya: Demo time: I'll send a request from the python client and show streaming responses.
[06:15] Maya: (typing) client.generate("Summarize: ...", stream=True) — streaming arrives as partial chunks; we also show chunked function call style.
[06:30] [06:35] Jordan: Nice. For function/tool calling — can we orchestrate with our lambda-based toolchain?
[06:41] Maya: Yes, function-calling maps to JSON schemas in our SDK, and you can configure webhook hooks to your lambdas.
[06:50] Priya: Any rate limits for sandbox? We want to run a small benchmark with 50 concurrent connections.
[06:56] Alex: Sandbox default limits are conservative; we'll bump them for the benchmark. We'll need to know your qps and sequence lengths.
[07:05] [07:15] Priya: We'll share a sample request trace. Expect average prompt length 80 tokens, with 120 token completions.
[07:21] Maya: Perfect. Optimize can take your traces and recommend batching/quantization to lower unit cost by x%.
[07:30] [07:40] Jordan: Can Optimize run offline on our traces or does it need live traffic?
[07:44] Maya: Both. You can upload traces to Console or run our CLI to simulate. It will produce a playbook: batching size, max batch latency, quantization profiles.
[07:55] Liam: Also note we have guardrails for quality monitoring — you can attach eval sets, and Optimize will alert on regressions.
[08:04] [08:15] Sam: On compliance: do you provide an SSP or SOC2 report for review?
[08:19] Alex: Yes, we'll send SOC2 Type II summary and an SSP redacted. We'll also include network diagrams for the VPC options.
[08:31] Sam: And where are customer logs stored? Are there PII retention windows?
[08:36] Maya: Logs retention is configurable; by default 30 days but enterprise packages allow 365 day. For private you control retention.
[08:48] [08:55] Priya: Walk us through env setup: we use GitHub Actions, want to inject secrets securely to runner.
[09:02] Maya: We recommend using repository secrets or Hashi Vault; our quickstart repo has examples for GH Actions with short-lived tokens.
[09:12] [09:20] (screen) Maya: TS quickstart: npm i @redwood/inference, add env var REDWOOD_KEY, then example: const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
[09:33] Jordan: Is there typed SDK for function responses?
[09:36] Maya: Yes, TS typings map function call schemas.
[09:41] [09:50] Priya: Ok, real talk on cost: do you have ballpark $/1k tokens for the recommended open models?
[09:56] Alex: Ballpark depends on model and quantization. For a typical 4-bit quantized mixture model on Dedicated you're looking at a meaningfully lower unit cost vs non-quantized. We'll send a model-cost sheet — rough ranges included.
[10:10] [10:15] Jordan: Could you show a quick Console flow to change a route's model and roll back?
[10:20] Maya: Sure — (screen) Route -> Versioning -> Create rollout. You can do canary 10% then full; Console records each rollout and you can set automatic fallback to previous if error rate rises.
[10:34] Priya: That fallback is critical for us.
[10:37] [10:45] Maya: Also note tracing hooks: you can send traces to your tracing backend or ours for correlation.
[10:53] Sam: For the benchmark, we might also need GPU affinity info and expected p95 for specific models. Can you provide perf numbers?
[10:59] Alex: We have verified perf profiles per model on the catalog; we'll share the perf sheet and we can run an in-house benchmark in our sandbox configured to mirror your sequence lengths.
[11:12] [11:20] Jordan: One last technical Q: how does continuous batching interact with KV cache for chatty sessions?
[11:26] Maya: Continuous batching uses per-session KV cache; for chat it's sticky and helps throughput without re-sending prefix. There's some nuance on cache eviction that we'll add to the docs.
[11:38] [11:45] Alex: Ok time check — about 35 minutes in. Let's cover next steps and owners.
[11:51] Priya: Perfect.
[11:54] [12:00] Alex: Recap: We'll send SOC2 + SSP, perf and model-cost sheet, sandbox keys for benchmark, and a quickstart repo link. Maya will run a follow-up technical call to set up the benchmark and pairing.
[12:12] Jordan: Great. When can we get the security docs?
[12:16] Alex: By EOD tomorrow.
[12:20] Sam: Can you also include KMS diagrams and BYOK notes?
[12:24] Maya: Yes — we'll include KMS diagrams and a simple flow for vault rotation.
[12:30] [12:35] Alex: Anything else from Cascade?
[12:39] Priya: No, that's it. Thanks.
[12:42] Alex: Thanks everyone, talk soon.

End transcript. (transcription quality: medium — some proper nouns/packagenames slightly garbled and timestamps approximate)
